column1: # Driver detection census (TRACKER §78) — MEASURED, never inferred.
# One row per assistant that has actually been observed driving this CLI. The
# rule the tracker states and this file enforces: "establish by running, not by
# reading, what each supported assistant actually exports". A named verdict in
# modules/system/manifest-driver.sh requires a row here first.
# tests/driver_detection.bats iterates these rows as positive controls: it sets
# ENV_PRESENT in a scrubbed environment and asserts EXPECTED_VERDICT. It also
# asserts the row count is non-zero, so an emptied fixture fails loudly rather
# than passing vacuously.
# ENV_PRESENT is `;`-separated. A NAME=VALUE pair is recorded only where the
# value is not secret and is itself evidence (an entrypoint, a version string);
# otherwise the bare NAME is recorded and the test sets it to 1.
# Columns:
#   ASSISTANT  HOST  DATE  OS  PS_FLAVOUR  ENV_PRESENT  ANCESTRY  TTY_IN/OUT  EXPECTED_VERDICT  RECORDED_BY
# ANCESTRY is the `comm` chain from the CLI's own shell outward, `,`-separated.
# TTY_IN/OUT is yes|no for stdin and stdout. Both are context for the next
# person: only ENV_PRESENT and EXPECTED_VERDICT are asserted.
# ABSENT SIGNALS MATTER TOO, and are recorded here because a candidate that
# turns out never to be set is what makes a detector work in a demo and fail in
# use. Measured absent on the claude-code row below: TERM_PROGRAM (§78 listed it
# as a candidate; it is not exported), and both stdin and stdout are NOT
# terminals — so the CLI's existing `[ ! -t 0 ]` check already classifies an
# agent-driven ship as non-interactive, and the interactive-human path can never
# fire under an agent. VSCODE_* is present but identifies the host EDITOR, not
# the driver: a human typing in the same terminal has it too, so it is never
# treated as agent evidence.
ASSISTANT
claude-code
